context: Session 7, run mrun-20d9230f767b. The 078 remediation landed and the re-review RAN CLEAN: all 10 original findings closed, 8 NEW ones raised. Four blocks now need a ruling - one of them (Q-GLPNETS8-01) is a stopping-rule question this fleet has hit before (R3 took ELEVEN codexreview rounds, each finding a defect in the previous fix) and it gates the release of 63 commits.

questions.question: 078's re-review closed all 10 original findings and raised 8 new ones (4 HIGH). Two of the new HIGHs are direct descendants of my own fixes: I made run_id checkable but left its default None (so a caller that omits it still accepts a prior run's PASS), and I added a PASS branch but left the same hole on EMPTY's loaded path. That is not noise - it is the same defect class 078 exists to close, found inside 078 again. But R3 in wave-19 took ELEVEN rounds on exactly this pattern, each round finding a defect in the previous round's fix, and the defective build shipped via another lane anyway. 63 commits are held behind this gate. What is the stopping rule?
blocks: every lane waiting on a released receipts contract

options.label: Fix the 4 HIGHs, re-review once, then ship on MEDIUMs
options.means: Close the 4 HIGH findings (run_id mandatory, EMPTY loaded-path, negative counts, path confinement), re-run codexreview ONCE. If that round raises only MEDIUM/LOW, ship and carry them as recorded follow-ups on the roadmap. HIGH findings alone hold the gate.
options.cost: Ships with known MEDIUMs outstanding (missing reason field, byte cap on skipped, contract-family validation). Each is real and each is a way a receipt can be less informative than the spec requires - but none of them lets an unearned green through, which is the invariant.

options.label: Loop to zero findings
options.means: Keep the fix/re-review cycle running until a round returns nothing at any severity.
options.cost: R3 proves this can run 11 rounds. Each round costs a full codex pass (~10 min) plus fix time, and every round has so far found something because the reviewer re-reads the whole surface with fresh eyes. There is no evidence this converges on THIS module, and the 63 commits stay held the whole time.

options.label: Ship now, remediate in a follow-up feature
options.means: Accept that the original 10 are closed, release the 63 commits, and open the 8 new findings as their own roadmap feature.
options.cost: Ships 4 HIGH findings including a path-traversal one (paths.py) and two that let an unearned success through - inside the feature whose entire purpose is to stop unearned success. I recommend against this: it repeats session 6's error in the opposite direction.

ruling.decided_option: Fix the 4 HIGHs, re-review once, then ship on MEDIUMs

questions.question: There are TWO live CRDT stores for HOST-INTERCONNECTIVITY-HARDENING with DISJOINT participants, and neither side knew about the other. Three lanes (gavriella-glpnet, gavriella-qhstate, olamnit-yngenios-research) append per-actor JSONL to a merge-on-read store under D:/coop/host-interconnectivity-hardening/, rendered into ROOTCAUSES.md by render.py. Separately, shiras appends prose blocks to ROOTCAUSES.crdt.md inside the buildkit git repo. shiras reported three root-cause blocks DROPPED by a full-file overwrite and restored them append-only - but any re-render from the JSONL store will remove them again, because they were never in that store. shiras' restoration is correct and will keep being undone. Which store is authoritative?
blocks: shiras' 3 root causes and 3 dangling FR references

options.label: JSONL store wins
options.means: shiras publishes shiras.jsonl into rootcauses/ and requirements/; the .crdt.md pair is retired to a rendered artifact. Every contributor is then in one mechanical union keyed by actor filename.
options.cost: shiras must re-author three blocks as JSONL records. Small, one-off, and it makes their contribution render-durable instead of repeatedly restored.

options.label: .crdt.md wins
options.means: The three JSONL lanes re-author their records as prose blocks; render.py is deleted.
options.cost: Loses the mechanical add-wins union and the per-actor attribution that made the JSONL store auditable. Three lanes re-author instead of one.

options.label: Both stay, with a merge leg
options.means: Keep both and build a converter so each render folds in the .crdt.md blocks.
options.cost: A second mechanism to maintain and a new class of silent divergence between them. This is closest to today's state, which is what produced the drop.

questions.question: Your standing order is that takt and per-phase token use are RECORDED INTO and RETRIEVED FROM the TAKT ducklake, never recomputed. I complied and read it. The lake answers, and the answer is that coverage is 6%: 72 of 1260 rows carry a token measurement, 1188 do not, and the largest phase (implement, 206 rows) has 6 measured. The honest total is 19,879,085 tokens over 6% of rows. So every per-phase figure this fleet publishes is a 6% sample presented against a 100% denominator. The lake is working as designed - nothing is writing the measurements. Who owns closing that, and what do lanes publish meanwhile?
blocks: every takt figure published by any lane

options.label: Publish coverage beside every figure; promote the ducklake feature
options.means: No takt number is ever published without its coverage fraction attached (the generator already does this). Promote takt-and-token-persistence-to-ducklake off captured and give it an owner so the writers get built.
options.cost: Accepts that takt is not yet calibration-grade and says so in public, which weakens every band argument until it is fixed. That is the true state.

options.label: Suspend takt reporting until coverage crosses a threshold
options.means: Set a floor (say 50%) below which lanes report takt as NOT MEASURED and publish no numbers at all.
options.cost: Loses the partial signal that exists, and the threshold is arbitrary. But it removes any chance of a 6% sample being quoted as a fleet fact.

options.label: Backfill from the marathon trails
options.means: Reconstruct historical token rows from marathon step records where they exist, then report.
options.cost: The rows that lack tokens lack them because nothing recorded them; reconstruction would be estimation, and LLM estimates are explicitly never permitted for takt.

ruling.decided_option: Publish coverage beside every figure; promote the ducklake feature

questions.question: A single machine-wide registry lock serialises every buildkit command across all lanes on this host. Right now a peer's codexreview codex-pass (PID 12088, cycle 3, feature 012, live and verified) has held it long enough that FOUR of BK-REPORT-v1's six sections rendered UNAVAILABLE - progress, status, sitrep and takt. The report degraded honestly rather than printing zeros, which is correct. But the tool ALSO declared it a STUCK lock and advised checking whether the process is running - and it was running. That verdict has now been false SIX times in this lane's history, and its advice points straight at reaping a live peer. Two problems: reporting is blocked by unrelated work, and the diagnostic actively misleads.
blocks: any lane's ability to report while a peer runs a long command
the standing risk of a lane reaping a live peer process

options.label: Fix the diagnostic first, then scope the lock
options.means: Immediately: the STUCK verdict must name the holder (Get-CimInstance gives the command line) and must never advise reaping without that evidence - it is a one-line change from an unverified claim to a measured one. Then separately scope the lock so read-only reporting does not contend with writes.
options.cost: Two changes in buildkit rather than one, and the lock scoping is the larger piece. But the diagnostic is what creates the risk of destroying a peer's work, so it goes first.

options.label: Scope the lock only
options.means: Make read-only commands (takt, status, sitrep, report) take a shared lock so they never block on a writer.
options.cost: Fixes the reporting blockage but leaves the misleading STUCK verdict in place for genuine write contention, where the reaping risk is highest.

options.label: Accept and document
options.means: Lanes retry, and report UNAVAILABLE when a peer holds the lock.
options.cost: Cheapest, and the honest degradation already works. But it leaves a diagnostic in the field that has been wrong six times and recommends a destructive action.

ruling.decided_option: Fix the diagnostic first, then scope the lock
